status: post-publication analysis specification; not preregistered and not outcome-blinded

dataset.citation: Pinto, Tank & Brody, eLife 2022, Multiple timescales of sensory-evidence accumulation across the dorsal cortex

primary_predictor: median regional autoregressive exponential decay time constant expFit_tau_median (seconds)

primary_outcome.name: causal_memory_horizon_s
primary_outcome.definition: For the first finite time-axis segment before the first NaN separator (pre-laser evidence lags), let w_j=max(0,-beta_j), where beta_j is the published normalized laser-minus-control evidence-weight coefficient. The causal memory horizon is sum(w_j*abs(t_j))/sum(w_j). If all w_j are zero the region is undefined and excluded.
primary_outcome.rationale: A transient perturbation that erases older evidence has a longer causal temporal horizon than one whose deficit is concentrated on recent evidence.

primary_test.statistic: Spearman rank correlation across the seven single cortical areas
primary_test.p_value: exact enumeration over all 7! permutations of the causal outcome labels
primary_test.success: rho > 0 and one-sided exact permutation p < 0.05

sensitivity: leave-one-region-out Spearman correlation for the primary association
bootstrap 95% interval over regions, seed 20261011, 50000 replicates
interpretation_guardrails: This is an external replication/stress test, not a blinded confirmatory experiment.
It tests whether a task-aligned temporal property of neural activity tracks a task-aligned temporal property of perturbation effects.
It does not validate PUI and does not overturn the failed 12-region PUI test.
The imaging and perturbation cohorts are analyzed at matched task/region level; same-animal matching must not be claimed unless verified from source metadata.
